The usual conditions were in force and two men were allowed in each event from each club, no man being allowed to turn out twice in the evening. 18 points were allocated to the winner's club, 17 points to second, and so on, downwards, in each event. The first race was at five miles and Redman (Metropolitan W.C.) and A.
Twenty walkers, including Alf Pope, 2nd claim, turned out for the Club 10 miles championship and handicap, and a match versus the Police made an added interest.
In 1930/1/2 he had many successes at these distances beating well known walkers of the day in C.W. Hyde, A.H.G.

The ex-holder favoured Alf Pope's preference for a steady 4¾ mph (13 minute miles) in which he is supported by Harold Whitlock.
